correctness.rationale: The decomposition AX=XH+R gives exact B=H+G11^{-1}G12 C. The epsilon near-isometry Gram condition yields the sharp mixing bound eps/sqrt(1-eps²) by a two-coordinate inequality. A direct real 2x2 singular-value/eigen-discriminant argument bounds imaginary parts at sqrt(max(0,delta²-(gap/2)²)); the explicit SPD 4x4 construction and a Gram matrix with (G-I)²=eps² I jointly attain the constants, including the defective collision. Exact rational identities and 20,000 deterministic spot checks independently corroborate essential finite algebra; analytic proof handles universal quantifiers and all equality cases.

originality.rationale: Liu and Liu (arXiv:2610.22261v1), Nakatsukasa and Tropp (arXiv:2111.00113), and the Hermitian-extraction comparison arXiv:2608.24529 were inspected at substantive relevant sections. None asserts the joint sharp eps–gap–residual real-spectrum transition with attained imaginary envelope. Searches of the research database and web for aliases and equivalent implications found no covering claim. The classic symmetric 2x2 perturbation threshold alone does not entail the sharp sketch Gram-block transfer bound or simultaneous positive-definite attainability. Residual risk of unindexed specialized prior results is acknowledged.

value.rationale: The exact safety boundary is a natural, sharp numerical-analysis question arising from possible complex Ritz pairs in symmetric sketched eigensolvers. It combines three intrinsic measurable quantities (sketch distortion, unsketched Ritz gap, residual norm) into a complete universal decision criterion, an exact nonreal error envelope, and a minimal SPD witness. This provides a principled criterion for whether real-Schur handling of complex pairs can become necessary, and is neither a renaming nor a known-table recomputation.
